title: The pro-étale site is subcanonical and its sheaves form a topos
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ its small pro-étale site
[def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site].

1. The pro-étale coverings [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] of objects of
   $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ satisfy the axioms of a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: isomorphisms are coverings; if
   $\{U_i\to U\}$ is a covering and $\{U_{ij}\to U_i\}$ are coverings, then
   $\{U_{ij}\to U\}$ is a covering; if $\{U_i\to U\}$ is a covering and $V\to U$ is a
   morphism of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, then the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] exist in
   $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}$ is a covering.
2. For every object $T$ of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ the representable presheaf
   $h_T=\Hom_X(-,T)$ is a sheaf; that is, the topology is subcanonical.
3. $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is essentially small in the larger universe $\mathcal V$ fixed by
   [def-weil-size-convention], and its category $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}};\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})$ of sheaves of
   $\mathcal V$-sets for its Grothendieck topology admits a $\mathcal V$-small-site
   presentation; equivalently, it is a $\mathcal V$-Grothendieck topos [def-weil-pbc-topos].

proof.text: Take base-change and composition stability of weakly etale morphisms from the unit-route theorem weaklyEtale_stability (sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability), installing both clauses as local instances. Then use the Mathlib realization of the same covering-axiom argument. The category X.ProEt and its finite limits are those of def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site. Its precoverage is the comap of proetalePrecoverage along the underlying-scheme functor. Mathlib proves that proetalePrecoverage has isomorphisms and is stable under composition and base change, using weakly etale stability and the quasi-compact jointly-surjective covering axioms (the fpqc operations of lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms). The forgetful functor preserves pullbacks, so Precoverage.comap transfers all three properties. Unfold ProEt.precoverage to expose these instances. Precoverage.toPretopology.transitive gives the required Presieve.bind composition clause; it explicitly reindexes both levels by their arrows. For an arbitrary indexed covering and morphism b, choose the categorical pullbacks pullback b (a i), use IsPullback.of_hasPullback, and apply Precoverage.IsStableUnderBaseChange.mem_coverings_of_isPullback. Thus the site axiom is proved for every Type (u+1) index set, including the empty one. This retains the unit's original covering-stability step and its named stability theorem; Mathlib implements the remaining precoverage operations.

proof.text: Use Mathlib's existing instance (ProEt.topology X).Subcanonical. Its proof is GrothendieckTopology.subcanonical_of_full_of_faithful applied to ProEt.forget X and the topology proetaleTopology.over X. The big proetale topology is subcanonical because it is bounded above by fpqcTopology, whose subcanonicity is exactly lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent. This formalizes the same fpqc descent argument, including the condition that maps are over X and the empty-cover case, through the full-and-faithful functor API.

The objects of X.ProEt lie in Type (u+1), and its morphisms lie in Type u, so Mathlib's essentiallySmall_of_small_of_locallySmall instance proves EssentiallySmall.{u+1} X.ProEt. Let e = equivSmallModel.{u+1} X.ProEt and K = e.inverse.inducedTopology (ProEt.topology X). SmallModel lies in Type (u+1) and has a SmallCategory instance in that universe. Apply Equivalence.sheafCongr with e and Type (u+1), the Mathlib realization of lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-sheaf-transport. Its inverse functor is a dense subsite automatically for this induced topology. This gives the required equivalence of the original sheaf category with sheaves on the small model.
